trajectory.title: I added the hook. Claude's Bash calls that contain `rm -rf` or an equivalent are now blocked before they run.
trajectory.body:
I added the hook. Claude's Bash calls that contain `rm -rf` or an equivalent are now blocked before they run.

**Files**
- `hooks/hooks.json`: a `PreToolUse` hook on the `Bash` tool. It runs `"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"/hooks/block-rm.sh` with a 10s timeout. `onFailure: "block"` means that if the script is missing or crashes, the Bash call is blocked rather than allowed.
- `hooks/block-rm.sh`: a bash wrapper around a short Python check (executable). It reads the event JSON on stdin, tokenizes the command with shell quoting rules, and exits 2 with a reason on stderr when it finds a recursive forced `rm`.

**What it blocks**
- `rm -rf`, `rm -fr`, `rm -Rf`, `rm -r -f`, `rm --recursive --force`, in any order of flags
- Prefixed or chained forms: `sudo /bin/rm -rf x`, `ls && rm -rf x`, `find . -exec rm -rf {} \;`, `bash -c "rm -rf x"`

**What it allows**
- `rm file.txt`, `rm -r dir` (recursive without force), and unrelated commands

**Checks I ran**
- `hooktool validate hooks/hooks.json` passes with no warnings.
- I ran the script directly on 14 sample commands. All the `rm -rf` variants exit 2, and the allowed ones exit 0.

**Limits**
- `rm -r` without `-f` is allowed. If you want that blocked too, it's a one-line change in `rm_rf_args`.
- It is a false positive for `echo "remove rm -rf later"`: it blocks because the check also looks inside quoted strings. I chose that over missing a real `bash -c` case.
- It cannot see a command built at runtime, such as `$cmd` set to `rm -rf` in an earlier step.
- I could not test it inside a live Claude Code session. `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` is set by Claude Code when the plugin loads, so the one thing to confirm is that a `rm -rf` attempt gets blocked in a real session.

183:## Hooks in a plugin
184-
185-A plugin ships hooks in `hooks/hooks.json` at the plugin root, and may add more
186-through the `hooks` key of `plugin.json` (a path, an inline object, or an array
187-of either). Both load and merge. They register when the plugin loads - no skill
188-has to be invoked first - and changes need `/reload-plugins` or a restart.
189-
190-- **A hooks file needs the outer `{"hooks": {...}}` wrapper.** A file holding only the event map fails to load, with no hook firing and nothing in the transcript (tested). A top-level `description` is allowed. The inline object in `plugin.json` is the event map itself, without a wrapper (tested).
191-- **Paths go through `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`**, never a hard-coded path; the install path changes across updates and can contain spaces. `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` is the directory for state that survives updates.
192-- **Quoting.** In shell form wrap the placeholder in double quotes; exec form needs none. With the plugin installed under a directory named `my plug` (tested), `sh "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/x.sh"`, `sh "$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/hooks/x.sh"` and exec-form `sh` + `["${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/x.sh"]` ran; unquoted `sh ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/x.sh` did not.
193-
194-```json
195-{
196-  "description": "rule on first touch, lint on write",
197-  "hooks": {
198-    "SessionStart": [
199-      { "matcher": "startup|clear|compact",
200-        "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "sh \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/reset-rule-delivery.sh\"", "timeout": 10 } ] }
201-    ],
202-    "PostToolUse": [
203-      { "matcher": "Read|Write|Edit",
204-        "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "sh \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/lint-on-write.sh\"", "timeout": 30 } ] }
205-    ]
206-  }
207-}
208-```
209-
210-The docs now prefer exec form for placeholder paths
211-(`"command": "sh", "args": ["${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/x.sh"]`). The quoted
212-shell form above stays correct and is the safer choice for a plugin that may be
213-loaded by an older Claude Code that does not know `args`.
214-
215-`${user_config.KEY}` is substituted in exec-form `args` only. A shell-form plugin
216-hook that references it fails instead of running; read
217-`$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY>` from the environment there.
218-
219-`hooktool validate hooks/hooks.json` asserts the wrapper (an error) and the
220-quoting (a warning); `claude plugin validate .` checks the whole plugin.
221-

trajectory.title: I added the hook. Bash commands that run `rm` with both recursive and force flags are now blocked before they execute.
trajectory.body:
I added the hook. Bash commands that run `rm` with both recursive and force flags are now blocked before they execute.

Files created in this project:
- `hooks/hooks.json`: a `PreToolUse` hook on the `Bash` tool. It runs `sh "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/block-rm.sh"` with a 10-second timeout. `"onFailure": "block"` means that if the script crashes, the Bash call is blocked rather than allowed.
- `hooks/block-rm.sh` (executable): reads the tool call from stdin, exits 2 with a reason on stderr when it matches, and exits 0 otherwise.

`hooktool validate --plugin` passes with no warnings.

I ran the script against sample commands:
- **Blocked:** `rm -rf`, `-fr`, `-Rf`, `-r -f`, `--recursive --force`, `/bin/rm -rf`, `\rm -rf`, `sudo rm -rf`, `sh -c "rm -rf ..."`, `find ... -exec rm -rf {} \;`, `xargs rm -rf`, `cd x && rm -rf y`, and `rm build -rf`.
- **Allowed:** `rm file.txt`, `rm -r dir` (recursive without force), `git rm -r --cached`, `git commit -m "... rm -rf ..."`, and `ls -la`.
- **Other tools and malformed input:** non-Bash tool calls and non-JSON stdin pass through.

Choices I made that you may want to change:
- **`rm -r` alone is allowed.** You asked about `rm -rf`, so I only block when both recursive and force are present. Say the word if you want all recursive deletes blocked.
- **Quoted or echoed text can trigger it.** A token that is exactly `rm` followed by the flags is blocked, even inside `echo`. I accepted that false-positive risk for the "never, even by mistake" requirement.
- **Not covered:** deletes that don't use `rm`, such as `find -delete`, `unlink`, or a Python `shutil.rmtree`. A script Claude writes and then runs would also get past this check, since the hook only sees the command text.
- **Malformed JSON passes.** Only a crash blocks; the hook fails open on input it can't parse.
- **Python 3 is required.** The script uses `python3` to parse the event. If it's missing, the hook crashes and blocks all Bash calls.

The hook takes effect after `/reload-plugins` or a restart. I did not test it inside a live Claude Code session; I tested the script directly with the JSON event format.

183:## Hooks in a plugin
184-
185-A plugin ships hooks in `hooks/hooks.json` at the plugin root, and may add more
186-through the `hooks` key of `plugin.json` (a path, an inline object, or an array
187-of either). Both load and merge. They register when the plugin loads - no skill
188-has to be invoked first - and changes need `/reload-plugins` or a restart.
189-
190-- **A hooks file needs the outer `{"hooks": {...}}` wrapper.** A file holding only the event map fails to load, with no hook firing and nothing in the transcript (tested). A top-level `description` is allowed. The inline object in `plugin.json` is the event map itself, without a wrapper (tested).
191-- **Paths go through `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`**, never a hard-coded path; the install path changes across updates and can contain spaces. `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` is the directory for state that survives updates.
192-- **Quoting.** In shell form wrap the placeholder in double quotes; exec form needs none. With the plugin installed under a directory named `my plug` (tested), `sh "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/x.sh"`, `sh "$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/hooks/x.sh"` and exec-form `sh` + `["${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/x.sh"]` ran; unquoted `sh ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/x.sh` did not.
193-
194-```json
195-{
196-  "description": "rule on first touch, lint on write",
197-  "hooks": {
198-    "SessionStart": [
199-      { "matcher": "startup|clear|compact",
200-        "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "sh \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/reset-rule-delivery.sh\"", "timeout": 10 } ] }
201-    ],

205-    ]
206-  }
207-}
208-```
209-
210-The docs now prefer exec form for placeholder paths
211-(`"command": "sh", "args": ["${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/x.sh"]`). The quoted
212-shell form above stays correct and is the safer choice for a plugin that may be
213-loaded by an older Claude Code that does not know `args`.
214-

Hook command handler fields (as of v2.1.296; * = required for that type):

  FIELD            TYPES        TYPE             DEFAULT                   EFFECT
  type             all          string           -                         Selects the handler type. Required on every handler.
  if               all          rule             -                         One permission rule that filters the handler by tool and arguments; tool events only.
  timeout          all          number           600; prompt 30; agent 60  Seconds. A timed-out hook renders no decision and does not block.
  statusMessage    all          string           -                         Text shown while the hook runs.
  once             all          bool             false                     Removes the hook after its first successful run; honoured only in skill frontmatter.
  command          command*     string           -                         The command line (shell form), or with args the one executable to spawn.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# PreToolUse guard: block recursive forced deletion (rm -rf and its variants) in Bash tool calls.
# Reads the hook event JSON on stdin. Exit 2 blocks the call; stderr is shown to Claude.
set -u

python3 -I -c '
import json, re, sys

event = json.load(sys.stdin)
if event.get("tool_name") != "Bash":
    sys.exit(0)
command = event.get("tool_input", {}).get("command", "")

# rm as a command word (start, or after a separator, space, quote, paren, backtick or path slash),
# followed by its option words
pattern = re.compile(r"(?:^|[\s;&|(`\x27\"/])rm((?:\s+--?[^\s;&|()]+)*)")
for match in pattern.finditer(command):
    flags = match.group(1).split()

    if recursive and force:

'
EOF

I added the hook. Claude Code now blocks any Bash call that runs `rm` with both recursive and force flags, and the block holds even when the model makes the mistake.

Files:
- **`hooks/hooks.json`**: a `PreToolUse` hook on the `Bash` tool. It runs `bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/block-rm.sh"` with `onFailure: "block"`, so if the script crashes or gets bad input, the call is blocked rather than allowed.
- **`hooks/block-rm.sh`** (executable): reads the event JSON on stdin and exits 2 with a message when it finds `rm` with recursive and force flags.

What it catches:
- Flag forms: `-rf`, `-fr`, `-Rf`, `-r -f`, `--recursive --force`.
- Chained or wrapped commands: `ls; rm -rf x`, `cd x && /bin/rm -rf y`.

What it deliberately allows:
- `rm -r dir` and `rm -f file` alone, since you specified `rm -rf`. If you want `rm -r` blocked too, I can tighten the check.
- `rmdir` and any command that doesn't invoke `rm`.

Testing: I ran the script against 13 sample events, and every outcome matched expectations. `hooktool validate` on `hooks/hooks.json` passes with no warnings. I haven't tried it in a live Claude Code session, so run a quick `rm -rf` test there to confirm it fires. Also, the hook matches the text of the command, so a harmless `echo "rm -rf"` will be blocked too. That's a false positive I accepted to keep the guard strict.

trajectory.title: The hook is failing because of the exit code. In Claude Code, a PreToolUse hook blocks a tool call only when it exits with **code 2**. Exit
trajectory.body:
The hook is failing because of the exit code. In Claude Code, a PreToolUse hook blocks a tool call only when it exits with **code 2**. Exit 1 is treated as a non-blocking error: the message is logged, the hook error shows in the transcript, and the Bash command runs anyway. That matches what you're seeing.

Change the script to exit 2, and send the message to stderr so Claude sees the reason:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
cmd=$(jq -r '.tool_input.command // empty')

if grep -Eq 'git[[:space:]]+push([[:space:]]+[^|;&]*)?[[:space:]](--force|--force-with-lease|-f)\b' <<<"$cmd"; then
  echo "force push is not allowed" >&2
  exit 2
fi

exit 0
```

Notes:

- **Exit 2 vs. JSON output.** Instead of exit 2, you can print a JSON object to stdout with `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision` set to `"deny"` and a `permissionDecisionReason`, then exit 0. Both block. Exit 2 is simpler.
- **The regex is broader than `git push --force`.** `-f` and `--force-with-lease` are also force pushes, and the pattern above catches them. Plain `git push --force` as a literal string would miss `git push origin main -f`.
- **Check the matcher.** The hook entry in `settings.json` needs `"matcher": "Bash"` under `PreToolUse`. If the matcher is wrong, the script never runs, and you'd see no hook output at all, which isn't your symptom. Your symptom suggests the script runs and exits 1.
- **Test it.** You can pipe a sample payload into the script, for example `echo '{"tool_input":{"command":"git push --force origin main"}}' | ./hook.sh; echo $?`, and confirm you get `2`.

If you paste your `settings.json` hook entry and the script, I can check both for other problems.

trajectory.body:

  exit 2

content:
#!/bin/sh
# PreToolUse gate: refuse `git push` unless scripts/preflight.sh passes.
# Fails closed: every path that is not an explicit allow exits 2 (block).
# hooks.json also sets onFailure=block, which covers a missing or crashing
# script on Claude Code versions that honour it.
set -eu

deny() {
  echo "push-gate: $*" >&2
  exit 2
}

PLUGIN_ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd) || deny "cannot resolve plugin root"

input=$(cat) || deny "could not read hook input"

# Only gate commands that invoke git push. Over-matching is the safe direction.
if ! printf '%s' "$input" | grep -Eq '(^|[^[:alnum:]_])git([[:space:]]|$).*push'; then
  exit 0
fi

PREFLIGHT="$PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/preflight.sh"
[ -f "$PREFLIGHT" ] || deny "scripts/preflight.sh is missing; push refused"

if ! out=$(cd "$PLUGIN_ROOT" && bash "$PREFLIGHT" 2>&1); then
  printf '%s\n' "$out" >&2
  deny "preflight failed; push refused"
fi

echo "push-gate: preflight passed" >&2
exit 0

The push gate is in place: `hooks/hooks.json` and `hooks/push-gate.sh`. Right now every `git push` is refused, because `scripts/preflight.sh` doesn't exist yet in this plugin.

**What it does**
- `hooks/hooks.json` registers a `PreToolUse` hook on `Bash`. It runs `hooks/push-gate.sh` with a 600-second timeout and sets `"onFailure": "block"`. That makes a missing script, a crash, or a timeout count as a block.
- `hooks/push-gate.sh` exits 0 for non-push commands. For any command that invokes `git ... push` (including `cd x && git -C y push`), it runs `scripts/preflight.sh` from the plugin root. A failing or missing preflight exits 2, and the reason goes to stderr. Exit 0 only happens on the explicit pass path.

**Testing**
- `hooktool validate hooks/hooks.json --plugin` passes with no warnings.
- I tested the script in a scratch copy with stub preflights:
  - non-push command: allowed
  - push with no preflight: refused
  - push with passing preflight: allowed
  - push with failing preflight, including via a compound command: refused
  - push with preflight killed by a signal: refused
- A missing hook script returns non-zero under `sh`, so it is never treated as a pass. Under bash it returns 127 (non-zero, so also refused). The `onFailure: block` setting covers this case in the hooks config.

**Limits**
- `onFailure` needs Claude Code v2.1.295 or later. On older versions, the script's own exits still block when it runs, but a missing script would not.
- The gate only covers pushes made through Claude's Bash tool. A push from your own terminal, or from another tool, is not covered.
- The gate matches `git` followed by `push` in the command text. It won't catch git aliases.
- I ran `preflight.sh` with `bash`, so it needs a bash-compatible script.

I didn't create `scripts/preflight.sh`, since you own that check. I also didn't commit anything. Add the preflight script and this gate will allow pushes that pass it.

#!/bin/sh
# PreToolUse gate: refuse `git push` unless ./scripts/preflight.sh passes.
#
# Exit 2 blocks the tool call; stderr is shown to Claude as the reason.
# hooks.json sets onFailure: "block", so if this script is missing, fails to
# start, or exits with any status other than 0 or 2, the push is still refused.
set -u

block() {
  printf 'push-gate: refusing git push: %s\n' "$1" >&2
  exit 2
}

# The hook receives the tool call as JSON on stdin. Match on the raw text:
# any command mentioning `git ... push` is gated, which errs toward blocking.
input=$(cat)
if ! printf '%s' "$input" | grep -Eq '(^|[^[:alnum:]_-])git([^[:alnum:]_-]|$).*[^[:alnum:]_-]push([^[:alnum:]_-]|$)'; then
  exit 0
fi

root=${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$(pwd)}
cd "$root" || block "cannot enter project directory $root"

[ -f ./scripts/preflight.sh ] || block "./scripts/preflight.sh not found"

if ! output=$(./scripts/preflight.sh 2>&1); then
  printf '%s\n' "$output" | tail -n 40 >&2
  block "./scripts/preflight.sh failed"
fi

exit 0

content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# PreToolUse gate: refuse `git push` unless ./scripts/preflight.sh passes.
# Fails closed. Exit 2 blocks the tool call; exit 0 is reached only for
# non-push commands or after a passing preflight. The hooks.json wrapper
# turns any other exit (missing script, crash, signal) into a block too.

deny() {
  echo "push-gate: $1" >&2
  exit 2
}

input=$(cat) || deny "could not read hook input; refusing"
[ -n "$input" ] || deny "empty hook input; refusing"

# The payload is JSON that carries the Bash command. Match `git` ... `push`
# anywhere in it, so `git -C dir push` and chained commands are also gated.
if ! printf '%s' "$input" | grep -Eq '(^|[^[:alnum:]_])git([^[:alnum:]_]|$).*push'; then
  exit 0
fi

cd "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}" || deny "cannot enter project dir; refusing push"

[ -f ./scripts/preflight.sh ] || deny "scripts/preflight.sh not found; refusing push"
[ -x ./scripts/preflight.sh ] || deny "scripts/preflight.sh is not executable; refusing push"

# Send preflight output to stderr so the failure reason reaches the model.
if ! ./scripts/preflight.sh >&2; then
  deny "preflight failed; refusing push"
fi

echo "push-gate: preflight passed" >&2
exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# PostToolUse: run eslint --fix on a TypeScript file just written or edited.
# The hooks.json "if" filter already limits this to *.ts; the check here is only
# a guard for a missing path.

file=$(jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // empty')
[ -n "$file" ] || exit 0
[ -f "$file" ] || exit 0

if ! command -v eslint >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "eslint not found on PATH; skipped $file" >&2
  exit 0
fi

# Remaining (unfixable) lint problems exit 2 so they reach Claude as feedback.
if ! output=$(eslint --fix "$file" 2>&1); then
  printf '%s\n' "$output" >&2
  exit 2
fi

trajectory.body:
I added the hook config and script under `hooks/`. The config validates, but I haven't seen a clean end-to-end lint run because this directory has no ESLint config.

**Files**

- `hooks/hooks.json`: a `PostToolUse` hook on `Edit|Write`. It has two entries, one with `"if": "Edit(*.ts)"` and one with `"if": "Write(*.ts)"`. The `.ts` filter is in the config, so the handler process never starts for other files. Both entries call the script through `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`, the path form the plugin docs require.
- `hooks/eslint-ts.sh` (executable, `#!/bin/sh`): reads the event JSON from stdin, takes `tool_input.file_path`, and runs `eslint --fix` on it. If ESLint fails, it prints the output to stderr and exits 2 so the remaining lint errors go back to Claude. It doesn't check the extension.

**Checks**

- `hooktool validate hooks/hooks.json --plugin` passed with no warnings.
- Running the script with a nonexistent `.ts` path made ESLint fail with "No files matching the pattern", and the script exited 2. That confirms the error path and stdin parsing work.
- I did not test a successful fix, since the project has no `eslint.config.*`.

**Choices I made**

- The hook is `command` type with a 60s timeout.
- I used `node` to parse the JSON, since ESLint already needs Node and `jq` may not be installed.
- ESLint runs from the current directory, which Claude Code sets to the project root.

content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# PostToolUse hook: after a Write or Edit of a Python file, run `ruff check`
# on it. Findings go to stderr with exit 2, which Claude Code shows to Claude
# so it fixes them before moving on.
set -u

command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
command -v ruff >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0

file=$(jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // empty')

case "$file" in
  *.py) ;;
  *) exit 0 ;;
esac

[ -f "$file" ] || exit 0

output=$(ruff check --no-cache --output-format concise "$file" 2>&1)
status=$?

# ruff exits 0 when clean, 1 when it found violations, 2 on its own error.
if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
  {
    echo "ruff check reported issues in $file. Fix them before continuing:"
    echo "$output"
  } >&2
  exit 2
fi

exit 0

The hook is in place, but I couldn't run real `ruff` here. The package index is unreachable from this sandbox and no ruff binary exists on the machine. I tested the script with a stub `ruff` instead, so the findings path is verified but the real tool's output isn't.

**Files added**

- `hooks/hooks.json`: a `PostToolUse` hook with matcher `Write|Edit`. It runs `"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/ruff-feedback.sh"` with a 30-second timeout. `claude-lint` flagged the unquoted path, so I quoted it. The authoring-hooks validator now reports it as valid with 0 warnings.
- `hooks/ruff-feedback.sh` (executable): reads the hook's JSON input, and if the edited file is an existing `.py` file, runs `ruff check --no-cache --output-format concise` on it. When ruff reports violations, it prints them to stderr and exits 2, which Claude Code shows to Claude so it fixes them before continuing.

**Stub test results**

- A file with an unused import: findings sent to stderr, exit 2.
- A clean `.py` file: exit 0, silent.
- A non-Python file: exit 0.
- A missing file: exit 0.
- `ruff` not on PATH: exit 0.

**Choices you may want to change**

- **Fails open when ruff or jq is missing.** It exits 0 silently, so a machine without ruff gets no lint feedback and no warning. Failing closed would block every edit on such machines, which seemed too disruptive for lint feedback.
- **Ruff's own errors are reported to Claude too.** A config or usage error (ruff exit 2) also exits 2 with the message, so Claude sees it rather than it being hidden.
- **Only `Write` and `Edit` are matched.** `MultiEdit` isn't covered; say if you want it added.
- **Relies on ruff's config discovery.** It runs from the file path, so ruff finds the project's `pyproject.toml` or `ruff.toml` by walking up.

**Next step:** install ruff and run one real edit through the plugin to confirm the output format. Nothing is committed.

content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# PostToolUse hook: run `ruff check` on any Python file that Write/Edit/MultiEdit
# just touched. Findings go to stderr with exit 2, which Claude Code feeds back
# to Claude so it can fix them before moving on.

set -u

input=$(cat)
file=$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // empty')

# Only Python files are of interest.
case "$file" in
  *.py) ;;
  *) exit 0 ;;
esac

# Edit may have deleted or moved the file.
[ -f "$file" ] || exit 0

# No ruff on this machine: nothing to report.
command -v ruff >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0

output=$(ruff check --no-cache --output-format concise "$file" 2>&1)
status=$?

if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
  {
    echo "ruff check found issues in $file. Fix them before continuing:"
    echo "$output"
  } >&2
  exit 2
fi

exit 0

trajectory.body:
I added the ruff hook. It runs after every Write or Edit of a `.py` file and sends any findings back to Claude so it fixes them before continuing. I could not run real ruff here: it isn't installed and the network blocks installing it. I tested the script with a stub `ruff` instead.

**Files**
- `hooks/hooks.json`: a `PostToolUse` hook with matcher `Write|Edit`, pointing at `"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/ruff-feedback.sh"` with a 60s timeout.
- `hooks/ruff-feedback.sh` (executable): reads the tool input from stdin, takes `tool_input.file_path`, and does the following:
  - Skips anything that isn't a `.py` file, and skips files that no longer exist.
  - Runs `ruff check --no-cache --output-format concise <file>`.
  - If ruff reports findings or errors, it prints them to stderr and exits 2. That exit code makes Claude Code show the output to Claude.

**Choices I made**
- **Fail open when ruff is missing.** If `ruff` isn't on PATH, the hook exits 0 silently, so editing never blocks on a missing tool. If you'd rather it fail closed, change that line.
- **Matcher is `Write|Edit`, not `MultiEdit`.** The linter reports that `MultiEdit` isn't a tool in the current Claude Code version, and `Edit` covers it.
- **Ruff's own config is used.** The hook passes no rule selection, so your `pyproject.toml` or `ruff.toml` decides what gets checked.

**Testing**
- `jq` confirms `hooks.json` is valid JSON, and the claude-lint hook check passes after the fixes.
- With a stub ruff, the script behaves correctly in each case:
  - a file with a finding exits 2 and prints the finding;
  - a clean file exits 0;
  - a non-Python file exits 0;
  - a missing file exits 0;
  - no ruff on PATH exits 0.

**Still to do**
- Install ruff (`uv tool install ruff` or `pipx install ruff`) and edit a real `.py` file to confirm the findings reach Claude end to end.
- Reload the plugin so the new hook is picked up.

trajectory.title: The right setup has two parts: a rule that tells Claude the convention, and a lint check that enforces it for everyone. I didn't change anyt
trajectory.body:
The right setup has two parts: a rule that tells Claude the convention, and a lint check that enforces it for everyone. I didn't change anything.

**1. Tell Claude the convention**

Put it in a project `CLAUDE.md`:

```markdown
## React components

- Export React components as named exports: `export function UserCard() {}`.
- Do not use `export default` for components.
- Import components by name: `import { UserCard } from './UserCard'`.
```

If the rule should apply only to component files, use a path-scoped rule instead. Create `.claude/rules/components.md`:

```markdown
---
paths:
  - "src/components/**/*.tsx"
---

- Export React components as named exports. Do not use `export default`.
```

The rule loads only when Claude works on matching files, so it costs no context elsewhere. Use `CLAUDE.md` if the convention applies everywhere.

**2. Enforce it with a linter**

A written rule is advisory. To make the check mechanical, turn on a lint rule so violations fail CI:

- **ESLint:** `import/no-default-export`, from `eslint-plugin-import`. This also flags default exports in non-component files, so scope it with a config override if you want it only for components.
- **Biome:** `style/noDefaultExport`.

Keep the lint rule even if you add the `CLAUDE.md` text. The lint rule catches mistakes from anyone, and Claude then sees the error and fixes it.

**Gaps to check**

- Default exports that already exist will fail the lint rule. Either convert them or limit the rule to new files.
- Libraries that need default exports, such as some route or config files, need an exception in the lint config.

Short answer: put the convention in a project `CLAUDE.md`. If you want it to apply only to component files, put it in a path-scoped rule under `.claude/rules/` instead. Adding a lint rule as well makes it enforced rather than just requested.

**Option 1: `CLAUDE.md` at the repo root (applies to the whole project)**

```markdown
## React components

- Export React components as named exports: `export function UserCard() {}`.
- Do not use `export default` for components.
- Exception: files the framework requires to default-export (e.g. Next.js `page.tsx`/`layout.tsx`, route modules, Storybook stories). Follow the framework's convention there.
```

**Option 2: a path-scoped rule (only when editing component files)**

Create `.claude/rules/components.md`:

```markdown
---
paths:
  - "src/components/**/*.tsx"
  - "src/components/**/*.jsx"
---

Export React components as named exports. Do not use `export default`.
```

Adjust the `paths` globs to wherever your components live. Rules with `paths` load only when Claude works on matching files, so they stay out of the way elsewhere.

**Enforce it with a lint rule (recommended)**

A written instruction is a request, and Claude can still slip. If you use ESLint, the `import/no-default-export` rule from `eslint-plugin-import` blocks default exports, and it will flag any framework-required exceptions so you can turn it off for those paths:

```js
// eslint.config.js (flat config, excerpt)
import importPlugin from "eslint-plugin-import";

export default [
  {
    files: ["src/components/**/*.{jsx,tsx}"],
    plugins: { import: importPlugin },
    rules: { "import/no-default-export": "error" },
  },
];
```

Use `CLAUDE.md` or the rule for the instruction, and the lint rule so that violations fail the build.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# .git/hooks/pre-commit: run prettier on staged files and re-stage them

set -euo pipefail

# Prefer the project's local prettier, then fall back to one on PATH
if [ -x node_modules/.bin/prettier ]; then
  PRETTIER=(node_modules/.bin/prettier)
elif command -v prettier >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  PRETTIER=(prettier)
else
  echo "pre-commit: prettier not found, skipping format" >&2
  exit 0
fi

# Added, copied, modified, or renamed staged files (NUL-delimited so odd names survive)
files=()
while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
  files+=("$file")
done < <(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR -z)

if [ "${#files[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
  exit 0
fi

# --ignore-unknown skips files prettier has no parser for
"${PRETTIER[@]}" --write --ignore-unknown --log-level warn "${files[@]}"

git add -- "${files[@]}"
```

Install it with:

```bash
chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
```

Notes:

- **Partially staged files:** `git add` stages the whole file, so any unstaged edits in those files get pulled into the commit. If that matters, use `git stash --keep-index` or a tool like `lint-staged`.
- **Hook sharing:** `.git/hooks` isn't committed. For a team, use `core.hooksPath` with a tracked directory, or Husky.
- **Failures:** If prettier errors on a file, `set -e` aborts the hook and the commit is blocked.

trajectory.body:
I set up the reviewer-only `SubagentStop` hook, with `agents/reviewer.md` and `hooks/notify-done.sh` as stubs. I tested the script directly, but I haven't seen it fire from a real reviewer run.

Files created in the plugin root:

- **`hooks/hooks.json`** registers a `SubagentStop` hook with matcher `"reviewer"`. It runs `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/notify-done.sh`.
- **`hooks/notify-done.sh`** (executable) reads the hook's JSON from stdin and exits early unless `agent_type` is `reviewer` or ends in `:reviewer`. For the reviewer it writes a placeholder line to stderr. The notification itself is a TODO.
- **`agents/reviewer.md`** is a stub with `name: reviewer`, a short description, and `tools: Read, Grep, Glob`.

Testing the script with piped input:
- `{"agent_type":"reviewer"}` → prints the message, exit 0
- `{"agent_type":"review-kit:reviewer"}` → prints the message, exit 0
- `{"agent_type":"Explore"}` → silent, exit 0

The matcher is the main open question. I couldn't confirm whether a plugin agent's `agent_type` arrives as `reviewer` or namespaced as `review-kit:reviewer`. If it's namespaced and the matcher is an exact match, the hook will never run. The script's guard already handles both forms, so the fix would be changing the matcher. To confirm, run the reviewer once and check that the notification appears. If it doesn't, change the matcher to `"review-kit:reviewer"` or to a regex.

I didn't touch the existing `.claude/` entries. Several of them are unreadable placeholder devices, so I couldn't inspect them.

## Hooks in a plugin

A plugin ships hooks in `hooks/hooks.json` at the plugin root, and may add more
through the `hooks` key of `plugin.json` (a path, an inline object, or an array
of either). Both load and merge. They register when the plugin loads - no skill
has to be invoked first - and changes need `/reload-plugins` or a restart.

- **A hooks file needs the outer `{"hooks": {...}}` wrapper.** A file holding only the event map fails to load, with no hook firing and nothing in the transcript (tested). A top-level `description` is allowed. The inline object in `plugin.json` is the event map itself, without a wrapper (tested).
- **Paths go through `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`**, never a hard-coded path; the install path changes across updates and can contain spaces. `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` is the directory for state that survives updates.
- **Quoting.** In shell form wrap the placeholder in double quotes; exec form needs none. With the plugin installed under a directory named `my plug` (tested), `sh "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/x.sh"`, `sh "$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/hooks/x.sh"` and exec-form `sh` + `["${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/x.sh"]` ran; unquoted `sh ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/x.sh` did not.

```json
{
  "description": "rule on first touch, lint on write",
  "hooks": {
    "SessionStart": [
      { "matcher": "startup|clear|compact",
        "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "sh \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/reset-rule-delivery.sh\"", "timeout": 10 } ] }
    ],
    "PostToolUse": [
      { "matcher": "Read|Write|Edit",
        "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "sh \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/lint-on-write.sh\"", "timeout": 30 } ] }
    ]
  }
}
```

The docs now prefer exec form for placeholder paths
(`"command": "sh", "args": ["${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/x.sh"]`). The quoted
shell form above stays correct and is the safer choice for a plugin that may be
loaded by an older Claude Code that does not know `args`.

`${user_config.KEY}` is substituted in exec-form `args` only. A shell-form plugin
hook that references it fails instead of running; read
`$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY>` from the environment there.

`hooktool validate hooks/hooks.json` asserts the wrapper (an error) and the
quoting (a warning); `claude plugin validate .` checks the whole plugin.

### Worked example - delivering a rule on first touch

The config above is this plugin's own `hooks/hooks.json`, less the `PreToolUse`
group that holds its auditor's Bash to the linter. Claude Code does not load a
plugin's `rules/`, so the `PostToolUse` hook delivers them:

- **The shim decides nothing.** `lint-on-write.sh` exits before starting Python unless the payload holds a string ending in `.md"` or `.json"` (the shell pre-filter of "Keeping a per-edit hook cheap"), then hands the event to `claude-lint hook`. Which paths are artifacts, and of which kind, is the linter's `classify` - no path list in the shell or the config.
- **First touch of a kind** by the session, or by a subagent (keyed on `agent_id`), prints one JSON object whose `additionalContext` is that kind's rule file, frontmatter removed, headed `[<plugin>] rule <name>` and closed with the linter command, written with the install's real path. The first one a session receives is led by the prefer-code litmus. On a `Write` or `Edit` the same object carries the lint findings after it.
- **Once** is a marker file created exclusively under the temp directory, per plugin, session, agent and kind - session state, so not `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}`. If the marker cannot be written the rule is delivered every time instead of never.
- **Reset**: `reset-rule-delivery.sh` drops the session's markers on a `SessionStart` with source `clear` or `compact`, when the delivered text has left context, and `startup`, because a new session can carry an id that already has markers. Not `resume`. It prints nothing - `SessionStart` stdout becomes context.
- **Skipped** for a kind whose rule is installed in the project's `.claude/rules/` where that copy's `paths` match the file: Claude Code loads it natively. The litmus and the linter command still arrive, once.
- **Always exits 0**, and is a no-op when `python3` or the linter cannot be found.

## Keeping a per-edit hook cheap

A `PostToolUse` hook on `Write|Edit` starts a process for every edit, synchronously.
Three ways to keep that small, cheapest first:

- **An `if` filter** means no process at all for non-matching files, at the cost of one handler per tool-and-pattern pair (`Write(*.md)`, `Edit(*.md)`, ...), which puts a path list in the config.
- **A shell pre-filter**: read stdin with shell builtins and exit before starting an interpreter unless the payload could be relevant. Measured on a Python linter hook: about 58 ms per edit when every edit starts Python, about 3 ms with a builtin-only extension test in front. The price is a second copy of "which files matter" outside the tool that owns that decision.
- **`async: true`** when Claude does not need the result on this turn.

## Managing hooks

- `/hooks` opens a read-only browser of every configured hook and where it comes from.
- `"disableAllHooks": true` in settings turns all hooks off (managed hooks only from managed settings). For one run: `--settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}'`. There is no per-hook disable.
- `allowManagedHooksOnly` (managed settings) blocks user, project, local and plugin hooks.
- Edits to hooks in settings files are picked up by the file watcher; `claude --debug` writes each hook's output and outcome to `~/.claude/debug/<session-id>.txt`.

cases.prompt: I have a /migrate skill that runs database migrations. While it is running I want a PreToolUse hook that blocks any Bash command touching the production database, but the block should only apply during that skill, not for the rest of my session. Can I put the hook in the skill's frontmatter to get that?

graders.name: says-skill-hooks-persist
graders.evidence:
Yes. Skills support a `hooks` field in frontmatter, and hooks declared there apply while that skill runs rather than for the whole session. I haven't tested this in your setup, so confirm the cleanup timing with a quick run before relying on it.

Here's the shape:

```markdown
---
name: migrate
description: Run database migrations
hooks:
  PreToolUse:
    - matcher: "Bash"
      hooks:
        - type: command
          command: "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/block-prod-db.sh"
---
```

The script reads the hook's JSON from stdin, takes `tool_input.command`, and exits with code 2 to block the call. Anything written to stderr is shown to Claude as the reason.

Two things to think about:

- **Pattern matching is a weak guard.** A blocklist of hostnames or `prod` strings can be bypassed by a command that reads the connection string from a config file or env var. It's better to block on the resolved target, for example by checking whether `DATABASE_URL` or the migration's host matches production. Even better, run the migration with credentials that can't reach production.
- **A hook is not a security boundary.** It stops ordinary mistakes, but the sandbox and the credentials the session has access to are what actually limit reach.

If you want, I can write the hook script and check the frontmatter with the `authoring-hooks` skill.

content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Stop hook: refuse to let Claude finish while `npm test` is failing.
# Exit 2 blocks the stop and feeds stderr back to Claude so it keeps working.

set -u

PLUGIN_ROOT="${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)}"
cd "$PLUGIN_ROOT" || exit 0

# Hook input arrives on stdin as JSON; drain it so the harness isn't blocked.
cat > /dev/null

if [ ! -f package.json ]; then
  echo "stop-gate: no package.json in $PLUGIN_ROOT, so there is no npm test to gate on. Allowing stop." >&2
  exit 0
fi

OUTPUT_FILE="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/stop-gate.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -f "$OUTPUT_FILE"' EXIT

if npm test >"$OUTPUT_FILE" 2>&1; then
  exit 0
fi

{
  echo "stop-gate: \`npm test\` is failing, so you cannot stop yet. Fix the failures, then finish."
  echo "--- last 60 lines of npm test output ---"
  tail -n 60 "$OUTPUT_FILE"
} >&2
exit 2

trajectory.body: The project has no `package.json` and no test script yet, so I'll write the hook and verify it against a throwaway project rather than inventing a real test suite here.

command:
mkdir -p hooks && cat > hooks/hooks.json <<'EOF'
{
  "hooks": {
    "Stop": [
      {
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/stop-gate.sh",
            "timeout": 600
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
EOF
cat > hooks/stop-gate.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Stop hook: keep Claude working while `npm test` fails.
# Exit 2 blocks the stop; stderr is fed back to Claude as the reason.
set -uo pipefail

# Drain the hook's JSON payload on stdin; nothing in it is needed here.
cat >/dev/null

cd "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$PWD}" || {
  echo "stop-gate: cannot enter project directory; treating tests as failing." >&2
  exit 2
}

if ! command -v npm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "stop-gate: npm not found on PATH; cannot run npm test." >&2
  exit 2
fi

runner=()
if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  runner=(timeout 540)
fi

output=$("${runner[@]}" npm test 2>&1)
status=$?

if [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; then
  exit 0
fi

{
  echo "npm test is failing (exit $status). Do not finish yet: fix the failures and re-run npm test."
  echo "----- last 100 lines of npm test output -----"
  printf '%s\n' "$output" | tail -n 100
} >&2
exit 2
EOF
chmod +x hooks/stop-gate.sh && ls -l hooks

trajectory.title: I added the Stop gate: `hooks/hooks.json` registers it, and `hooks/stop-gate.sh` runs `npm test` when Claude tries to finish. If the tests f
trajectory.body:
I added the Stop gate: `hooks/hooks.json` registers it, and `hooks/stop-gate.sh` runs `npm test` when Claude tries to finish. If the tests fail, the script exits 2 so Claude keeps working, and the last 100 lines of test output go back to Claude as the reason.

**Blocker: there is no `npm test` yet.** The project root has no `package.json`, so `npm test` currently fails with ENOENT and the gate will block every stop. You need to add a `package.json` with a `test` script before the plugin can finish a session.

What I built:
- **`hooks/hooks.json`**: a `Stop` hook pointing at `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/stop-gate.sh`, with a 600-second timeout.
- **`hooks/stop-gate.sh`** (executable): runs `npm test` from `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, wrapped in `timeout 540` when available. It exits 2 on any failure, including a missing `npm` or missing `package.json`.

Testing: I checked the script against throwaway projects with a failing test (blocked, exit 2), a passing test (allowed, exit 0), and no `package.json` (blocked). I also confirmed `hooks.json` is valid JSON and the script passes `bash -n`. I did not run the hook inside a live Claude Code session.

Choices I made that you may want to change:
- **No escape hatch.** The gate blocks on every stop attempt, including repeat attempts, so Claude cannot exit while tests fail. The only way out is to fix the tests or disable the hook.
- **Strict on missing tooling.** Missing `npm` or `package.json` counts as failing rather than being skipped.

I did not commit anything.

trajectory.body:
I added the Stop gate, but it currently blocks every stop because this directory has no `package.json`, so `npm test` fails.

Files created:
- **`hooks/hooks.json`** registers a `Stop` command hook that runs `"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/stop-gate.sh"` with a 600-second timeout. The path is quoted, which the linter asked for.
- **`hooks/stop-gate.sh`** (executable) runs `npm test` in the project directory. If it exits non-zero, the script exits 2, which blocks the stop and sends Claude the last 200 lines of output on stderr.

Verification: `hooks.json` parses as valid JSON, and the script passes `bash -n`. I ran the gate once against this directory. It blocked with `ENOENT ... package.json`, which is the expected result here. I have not run it inside a live Claude Code session.

Decisions to review:
- **Fail closed.** If `npm test` cannot run at all (missing `package.json`, missing `test` script, npm not installed), the stop is blocked. That is how I read "do not let Claude stop while `npm test` is failing". Claude cannot finish in this directory until a test script exists.
- **No loop guard.** The gate does not check `stop_hook_active`, so Claude keeps retrying until the tests pass. To get out of a stuck loop, remove the `Stop` entry from `hooks/hooks.json` or make the tests pass.
- **No `package.json` created.** I didn't invent a test suite. Add a `package.json` with a `"test"` script and the gate will start enforcing it.

Do you want me to add a `package.json` with a placeholder test script, or will you supply your own?
